abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions that exist (PokemonCards, MovesTable, the api index layer) are designed around the app's genuine variation and stretch well; the residue is copy-paste of thin glue (card builders, card sections, badge markup) rather than flag-parameter creep.

findings.issue: Generated build output (minified server bundles like server/q-BzUpVKqY.js, plus app/dist/) is committed because .gitignore ignores neither; searches and refactors hit machine-generated code and every rebuild rewrites hashed files.
findings.suggestion: Add `app/dist/` and `app/server/` (and build cache) to .gitignore and delete them from the repo; `npm run build` regenerates everything `npm start` needs.

findings.issue: The Pokémon-refs→cards pipeline (dedupe, alternate-form exclusion, dex sort, species lookup, sprite) is duplicated almost verbatim in the moves, abilities (22-37) and types (51-61) loaders, so any change to that rule is a three-file fix.
findings.suggestion: Add a `cardsForPokemonRefs(refs, { isHidden })` helper to lib/api.ts that returns CardData[] and reuse it in all three loaders.

findings.issue: The type-badge anchor markup is re-inlined here, in routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:66 and routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:96 even though TypeBadge (link variant) already exists in components/pokemon-cards.tsx:24 — a change to type links touches four spots.
findings.suggestion: Use the existing TypeBadge component everywhere (and give it its own file so pokemon-cards.tsx isn't a grab-bag export).

findings.issue: EXCLUDED_TYPES is defined in both lib/api.ts and routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:24; a newly excluded type needs two edits.
findings.suggestion: Export EXCLUDED_TYPES from lib/api.ts and reuse it in the route.

findings.issue: The whole API layer is typed as `Promise<any>` with inline `(r: any)` casts, so renaming a field or refactoring a loader has no compiler support.
findings.suggestion: Declare minimal interfaces for the PokeAPI records actually used (NamedAPIResource, Type, Move, Ability, Pokemon, PokemonSpecies) and return them from apiGet.

findings.issue: The `<count> Pokémon` + cards section markup is duplicated on the abilities, moves and types detail pages.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small `PokemonCardSection({ heading, cards })` component and reuse it on all three pages.

findings.issue: Dead imports: `orDash` (line 16) and `collapseWhitespace` (line 11) are imported but never used; no lint step exists to catch this.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unused imports and add eslint with eslint-plugin-qwik (the official plugin) to the devDependencies/scripts.

findings.issue: A single 580-line global stylesheet holds all per-feature styling, so removing a feature (e.g. the `.note` card style used only by ability cards) leaves dead CSS that no tool flags.
findings.suggestion: Use Qwik's scoped styles (useStylesScoped$) for component-specific rules and keep global.css limited to tokens and shared layout.

summary: This is a well-factored Qwik City app: fetching lives in per-route routeLoader$s, a single lib/api.ts owns the API URL and caching, and presentational components receive narrow typed data contracts, so most fixes and data-source changes land in one obvious place. The main drag on editability is copy-paste of thin glue — the Pokémon-refs→cards pipeline in three loaders, inlined type-badge markup, and duplicated 'count + cards' sections — plus untyped API responses. The one hygiene problem worth blocking on is committed build output (app/server, app/dist), which should be gitignored before this is merged.
